issues.description: The problem statement requires Book to provide a method description() -> String that returns the book's details (problem_statement.md lines 17-19). In the solution, Book.description() is implemented as func description() { print("...") } — it returns Void and prints directly to stdout instead of returning a String (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 34-36). This is a signature/behavior mismatch: students implementing description() -> String (as specified) will find the solution's implementation inconsistent and tests or example usage that expect a returned String would not match the solution. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected method contract and how to use description() in client code.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the implementation consistent with the problem statement: change Book.description() in the solution to have the signature func description() -> String and return the book details (e.g. return "\(title) by \(author)"). Update any client code that currently relies on description() printing directly to use the returned String when printing. Alternatively, if the intended design was for description() to print, update the problem statement to require description() -> Void and describe the printing behavior — but keep one clear contract across artifacts.
